1.explanation:
• ComboBox.js: This functional component defines all of the input rendering, Downshift integration, and prop handling. To implement readOnly, you must extend its propTypes (add readOnly), defaultProps, and the JSX for the <input> (pass through readOnly=props.readOnly, add CSS class, and guard any toggle or filter behaviors when readOnly). Without touching ComboBox itself, the prop will not change behavior or styling.

• ComboBox.stories.js (Playground): In order to surface the new readOnly control in Storybook and allow designers/developers to test/readOnly states, the Playground story (and default export argTypes) must include readOnly with a boolean control and be spread into the <ComboBox> in the story.

• ComboBox-test.js: There are currently no RTL tests for readOnly. To ensure this new prop works (e.g. input has attribute readonly, does not fire onChange/onToggle, and does not open the menu), new test cases must be added to ComboBox-test.js under a describe(‘when readOnly’, …) block. This solidifies readOnly as a supported, tested feature.
1.bug_scenario: The user wants the Carbon React ComboBox to support a new readOnly prop that matches the design specs shown in the images — a non-editable but focusable input with specialized styling (e.g. placeholder/text colors, cursor, spacing around icons) and no menu expansion when clicking the input. Currently passing readOnly to <ComboBox> has no effect.

2.explanation: 1. ComboBox (in ComboBox.js): The core functional component must be updated to read the new `readOnly` prop, block text input and menu toggle, and apply the correct read‐only CSS class for styling. 2. ComboBox.propTypes & ComboBox.defaultProps: We need to declare `readOnly: PropTypes.bool` (defaulting to false) so the prop is documented, type‐checked, and participates in default behavior. 3. Playground (in ComboBox.stories.js): The story that drives the interactive playground must expose the `readOnly` boolean control and include a default example for easy copy/paste. 4. ComboBox-test.js: New RTL tests should be added to verify that when `readOnly` is true, the input cannot be edited, the expand toggle is disabled, and the correct `read-only` class or attribute is rendered to satisfy acceptance criteria.
2.bug_scenario: The user wants to render a read‐only version of the ComboBox (i.e. when `readOnly={true}`) that matches the Carbon spec (no input text changes, no menu toggle, special read‐only styling and icon behavior). The provided screenshot shows the visual spec for both the empty and filled read‐only states (fixed spacing, disabled icon color, transparent border, gray text). Currently, the ComboBox component does not honor a `readOnly` prop—typing is still allowed and the menu can still expand.
